summary:
OrbitCraft is a browser-based spacecraft systems engineering simulator developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 to bridge the gap between oversimplified space games and inaccessible professional CAD tools. The platform tasks users with designing modular satellites and probes that balance authentic, interdependent aerospace constraints: structural mass budgets, propulsion (calculated via the Tsiolkovsky Rocket Equation), inverse-square solar radiation, battery eclipse depth of discharge, RF data links, and mission procurement costs across four progressive interplanetary envelopes.

To address the educational challenge, OrbitCraft turns theoretical physics into active problem-solving through an automated Flight Readiness Review console with real-time engineering advisories, dynamic 2D Keplerian orbital trajectory visualization (Apoapsis/Periapsis), and an interactive multi-stage launch ascent featuring synthesized Web Audio rocket roar, Max-Q aerodynamic pressure alerts, stage separation, and fairing jettison.

OrbitCraft is important because it delivers high-fidelity aerospace education with zero barriers requiring no installations or specialized hardware. Grounded in NASA Systems Engineering standards (SP-2016-6105) and planetary factsheets, it provides students, educators, and aspiring engineers worldwide with an open-access testbed to intuitively master the real-world trade-offs of modern space mission design.
details:
Project Mechanics & How It Works

OrbitCraft is an interactive, browser-based spacecraft systems engineering and mission design simulator. Users assume the role of a flight systems architect tasked with designing, validating, and flying modular spacecraft across four progressive mission envelopes: Low Earth Orbit observation (TerraWatch-1), Lunar polar reconnaissance (SeleneMapper), Mars aeronomy (AresAtmosphere), and deep-space outer planet exploration at Jupiter (Jovian Odyssey).

The platform operates via a real-time, deterministic aerospace physics engine:

  • Mass & Structural Margins: Every subsystem added (bus frames, payloads, power, avionics, propulsion, and telecommunications) contributes to the dry and wet mass budgets, directly impacting launch vehicle margins.
  • Tsiolkovsky Rocket Equation: Calculates orbital velocity margins based on engine Specific Impulse and propellant mass fraction.
  • Inverse-Square Radiation & Thermal Dynamics: Photovoltaic power yields scale inversely with heliocentric distance, requiring transition to nuclear Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators (RTGs) in outer planetary environments.
  • Eclipse Power & Storage: Simulates dark-pass battery depth-of-discharge (DoD) during planetary shadows to avoid catastrophic subsystem brownouts.
  • RF Downlink & Telemetry Buffers: Models data collection rates against antenna downlink bandwidth, utilizing onboard Solid-State Recorders (SSRs) to prevent data overflow.
  • Automated Flight Readiness Review (FRR): A diagnostic advisory system evaluates system architecture against mission requirements in real time, pinpointing engineering deficits and recommending corrective subsystem allocations.
  • Orbital Trajectory & Launch Simulation: Features an interactive 2D Keplerian orbit canvas derived from the Vis-Viva equation (propagating Apoapsis and Periapsis dynamically) and a multi-stage flight ascent sequence incorporating transonic Max-Q aerodynamic pressure alerts, stage separation, vacuum plume expansion, and fairing jettison.

    Project Benefits & Intended Impact

Traditional aerospace mission design is bifurcated into two extremes: oversimplified arcade games that disregard the laws of physics, or high-barrier, license-restricted CAD and trajectory simulation software inaccessible to aspiring students.

OrbitCraft bridges this gap by delivering:

  • Zero-Barrier Aerospace Education: Entirely client-side and web-based, requiring no high-end hardware, desktop installations, or specialized licenses.
  • Systems Engineering Literacy: Teaches players that spacecraft design is fundamentally an exercise in interdisciplinary trade-offs—increasing science payload mass demands more propellant, which escalates electrical consumption, requiring heavier solar arrays, ultimately degrading orbital insertion margins.
  • Global Classroom Utility: Serves educators and STEM students worldwide as an experiential digital laboratory where abstract aerospace formulas (orbital mechanics, link budgeting, power curves) become immediately observable, interactive systems.

Tools, Languages, Software & Hardware Used

  • Core Framework: React 18, Vite build tooling, JavaScript (ES2023).
  • UI/UX & Visualization: Tailwind CSS for responsive mission control consoles, Lucide React for aerospace iconography, and HTML5 Canvas API for deterministic 2D Keplerian orbital propagation.
  • Audio Synthesis: Web Audio API (custom algorithmic synthesizers generating real-time low-frequency rocket rumble noise, bandpass launch soundscapes, and flight computer telemetry cues without external audio asset overhead).
  • Version Control & Deployment: Git, GitHub for open-source repository management, and Vercel Serverless Edge Platform for global zero-latency hosting.
  • Hardware Environment: Developed and tested on standard consumer-grade laptops (Acer Aspire Lite 15) to guarantee lightweight performance on budget educational hardware.

Creativity & Innovation

OrbitCraft merges rigorous mathematical fidelity with engaging, mission-critical gamification:

  1. Interactive Subsystem Interdependency: Rather than static quiz-based learning, every component choice actively alters downstream electrical, thermal, RF, and trajectory telemetry.
  2. Procedural Web Audio Engine: Instead of playing generic pre-recorded mp3 sound loops, OrbitCraft synthesizes realistic rocket combustion roar dynamically using oscillator arrays and white noise filters that respond to altitude and atmospheric pressure changes.
  3. Flight Director Advisory System: Converts dry validation errors into intelligent, actionable aerospace engineering hints, guiding learners through structured troubleshooting rather than frustrating dead-ends.
  4. Authentic Launch Sequencing: Accurately visualizes staging mechanics, shifting from Sea-Level atmospheric combustion to Upper-Stage vacuum hydrolox expansion, accompanied by fairing separation at Karman boundary regimes.

Key Engineering Factors & Design Considerations

  • NASA Data Grounding: Component specifications, planetary solar irradiance constants, and gravitational parameters ($\mu$) were directly derived from NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) Planetary Fact Sheets.
  • Aerospace Systems Standards: The Flight Readiness Review workflow, subsystem categorization, and margin philosophy follow the guidelines established in the NASA Systems Engineering Handbook (SP-2016-6105 Rev 2).
  • Acoustic & Aerodynamic Profiling: Launch stress indicators, Max-Q dynamic pressure thresholds, and stage separation criteria incorporate flight mechanics literature from the NASA SP-8000 Space Vehicle Design Criteria series.
  • Universal Accessibility: Strict optimization for low network bandwidth, minimal memory footprint, and cross-platform compatibility across modern mobile and desktop browsers.
